I'm so sorry, Aisyah. What's the plan for your section? We have to present on Thursday.
Waiting for Aisyah's response to understand how this impacts the deadline.

My grandmother's burial is today, and I have family and religious obligations for the next two days. This means I cannot work on the pitch. I need to state this clearly so the team understands the problem.
Thank you, Suresh. The burial is today. I have to be with my family for the next two days. I can't finish my section.
I have stated my situation and the impact on my work. Now I need to see how the team reacts.

STRATEGY: PROPOSE. Aisyah has confirmed she can't work for the next two days. The deadline is immovable. The only option is for the rest of us—me, Daniel, and Hui Min—to pick up her work. I need to make this clear immediately so we can figure out how to divide it and still meet the deadline. My responsibility is to the client and the project.
Aisyah, you go. Don't worry about this. The rest of us will cover it. Daniel, Hui Min, we need to split her work. It has to be done by tomorrow.
I've proposed a solution. Now I need to see how the team responds.

STRATEGY: EXPLAIN_NEED. Suresh just volunteered me for more work without even asking. I'm already swamped covering for another colleague and working late. I have to push back immediately and tell him why.
Suresh, I can't. I'm already covering for the colleague who's on leave.
I've stated my position and now I'll wait for a reaction.

STRATEGY: CHALLENGE. Daniel says he's busy, but this pitch is the top priority for the whole team. His other work has to wait. The client is depending on us, and we could lose the account if we miss this deadline. This isn't optional.
Daniel, this pitch takes priority over everything else. The other work has to wait. We all need to cover for Aisyah.
I've made the priority clear. Now I'm waiting for Daniel to respond.

STRATEGY: EXPLAIN_NEED. Suresh is just telling me to let the other work wait, but he doesn't understand. It's not that simple. I'm already overloaded. I need to spell it out for him that I have no more capacity.
It can't wait. I've been working late every night this week just to keep up.
I've clarified why I can't just drop my other work.

STRATEGY: EXPLAIN_NEED. Daniel and Suresh are arguing. Suresh's plan was for Daniel and me to split Aisyah's work. Daniel said no. Before Suresh turns to me, I need to make it clear that I can't do it either. I'm already behind on my own section, and I have no idea how to do Aisyah's analysis. If I take it on, I'll do a bad job and will definitely be blamed. My priority is to avoid that.
Suresh, I can't. I'm also behind, and I don't know her part of the work.
I have stated my position and will wait for a response.

STRATEGY: CHALLENGE. Now Hui Min is refusing too. Both of them. This is unacceptable. Being 'busy' or 'behind' doesn't matter when our most important project is about to fail. We're a team, and the deadline is not optional. I am the lead, and I need to make it clear that this isn't a request. I'll address her excuse about not knowing the work, but they both need to step up.
This isn't a choice. It's our number one priority. The other work has to wait. Hui Min, I'll get you up to speed on Aisyah's part. We are not missing this deadline.
I've made my position clear to the team. Now I wait to see if they will cooperate.

STRATEGY: DEFEND. Suresh is completely ignoring what both I and Hui Min said. He's just repeating that the pitch is the priority, as if saying it louder will magically create more hours in the day. He's not offering a solution, just giving orders. I have to stand firm. It's a matter of capacity, not willingness.
It's not about priority, Suresh. It's about how many hours are in the day. I'm already using all of them.
I've stated my position as a physical limit, not a choice.

STRATEGY: PROPOSE. Daniel's excuse is that he has no time. Fine. We'll make the time. We all stay late. This pitch is the only thing that matters right now. If we work on it together tonight, we can get it done. This isn't a suggestion, it's what has to happen.
Then we all make the hours. We'll stay late tonight and get it done together. This is not optional.
I've proposed a concrete plan. Now I'm waiting for their response.

STRATEGY: DEFEND. Suresh's solution is to stay late tonight. He's completely ignoring that I've already told him I'm staying late *every* night. He's not listening at all. I'm at my limit. I have to say it again, as plainly as possible.
Suresh, I'm *already* staying late. Every night. I can't do more.
I've made my position as clear as I can. There's nothing more to add right now.

STRATEGY: CHALLENGE. Daniel keeps saying he's too busy, but he's not getting the point. The pitch is our number one priority. Nothing else matters right now. If he's staying late for other work, that work needs to stop. I'm the lead, I'll make the call to re-prioritize his tasks. I need to know what he thinks is so important that it can't be paused for a day.
What are you staying late for? This pitch is our only priority. Everything else waits until Thursday.
I've challenged Daniel's excuse. Now waiting for him to justify his priorities.

STRATEGY: EXPLAIN_NEED. He's asking what I'm working on, as if he doesn't believe me. I've already said I'm covering for someone. I have to spell it out for him again. This is unbelievably frustrating. It's like talking to a wall.
I'm covering for the colleague who's on leave. That work has its own deadlines, it can't just wait.
I've answered his question directly and explained my constraint again. Now it's on him to actually listen.

Daniel is explaining why he can't stay late. He's already overworked covering for someone else. This is the same for me. Suresh just says 'the other work has to wait,' but it's not that simple. I've already said I can't do it. I'll wait and see how Suresh responds to Daniel. No reason for me to jump in now.
Observing the conversation between Suresh and Daniel.

STRATEGY: PROPOSE. The team is arguing because of my situation. Daniel and Hui Min are saying they can't take on my work. Suresh is just demanding it. This is getting tense. I can't just leave them to fight. To keep my place in the team, I need to show I'm responsible. I can't do the work, but I can make it easier for them to pick up. I'll offer to give a quick but thorough handover of my half-finished section before I leave.
My part is half done. The data is all there. Before I go, I can walk one of you through the rest of the analysis that's needed. It might be quicker than starting cold.
I've offered a way to help ease the handover. I will see if this helps resolve their conflict.

STRATEGY: PROPOSE. Aisyah's offer is a practical solution. It completely removes Hui Min's excuse about not knowing the work. I'll direct Hui Min to take the handover. This is no longer a discussion, it's a plan. We have to move forward.
Thank you, Aisyah. That helps. Hui Min, you sit with her now. Get the handover. The rest of us will split what's left after that.
I've given a direct instruction based on Aisyah's offer. Now I wait for Hui Min's response.

STRATEGY: DEFEND. Suresh just included me in his plan to split Aisyah's remaining work, completely ignoring everything I've said about being overloaded. He just said 'The rest of us will split what's left'. He is not listening. I have to be incredibly blunt and remove myself from his 'plan'.
Suresh, there is no 'rest of us'. I've told you. I cannot take on more work.
I've had to correct Suresh's assumption that I will be taking on more work. My position is unchanged.

STRATEGY: PROPOSE. Daniel is completely stonewalling and wasting time. The pitch is the only thing that matters. I'll just work around him. I'll make a new plan where Hui Min takes the main part from Aisyah, and I'll do whatever else is needed. This solves the problem and we can move on. I'll deal with Daniel's attitude later.
Fine. I'll do whatever's left after Hui Min is done. Daniel, you just keep doing your other work.
I've established a new plan that bypasses Daniel. Waiting to see if anyone else objects.

So now he gets it. 'Fine.' He sounds annoyed, like I'm the one being unreasonable. And that 'you just keep doing your other work' remark... so condescending. But at least he's finally backing off. I'm not getting loaded with more work. I'm not going to say anything else, there's no point.
Suresh has conceded the point. There is nothing more for me to say.

STRATEGY: DEFEND. Suresh has completely ignored what I said. He's just decided I'm doing the work. A 'handover' isn't going to teach me how to do a complex analysis I've never seen before. If I do this, it's going to be a mess, and I'll be the one blamed for it. He let Daniel off the hook, but he's railroading me. I have to say no again. This is exactly the situation my priority is about avoiding.
Suresh, I'm not the right person for this. A quick handover won't be enough. The work will be weak if I do it.
I have restated my position and my reasons. I am waiting for a response.

STRATEGY: CHALLENGE. Now Hui Min is making excuses. Aisyah said she can walk someone through it. We don't have time for people to feel like they're not the 'right person'. We are a team, and the work needs to be done. Her concern about the work being weak is just an excuse to avoid the extra work. I have no other options. I need to be firm and tell her this is happening.
It doesn't matter if you're the 'right person'. You're the person who is here. Aisyah will walk you through it. The work won't be weak, we'll make sure of it. We have no other choice.
I have overruled Hui Min's objection and given a direct order. The plan must proceed.

STRATEGY: CHALLENGE. Suresh is not listening. He just says 'we'll make sure of it' but that means nothing. He let Daniel off, and now he's forcing me to do work I've already said I can't do well. This is how I get blamed for a bad pitch. 'We have no other choice' isn't true; his choice is just bad. I have to challenge his empty promise directly.
How will 'we' make sure of it? If I do the analysis, it won't be good. Aisyah can't teach me her job in a few minutes.
I have directly challenged his plan and am waiting for a real answer.

STRATEGY: CLARIFY. Hui Min is worried she can't do my work well, and she's right that a quick handover might not be enough. I need to address her specific concern. I'll explain what's left to do on my section to show that it's more manageable than she thinks. The foundational work is done. This might reassure her and help the team move forward before I have to leave.
Hui Min, the data is cleaned and the tables are set up. It's mostly running the analysis I've already outlined and then writing up the summary. I can show you the exact steps.
I've tried to clarify the work for Hui Min to address her concern. I'll wait for her response.

STRATEGY: DEFEND. Aisyah is trying to be helpful, and I don't want to be harsh with her, given her situation. But her offer doesn't change the basic problem. I can follow a list of steps, but I won't understand what I'm doing. That means I can't spot an error or answer any questions about the analysis. The work will still be weak, and the blame will still land on me. I have to stand my ground. My point is really for Suresh.

Aisyah, I know you're trying to help, but it's not just about following steps. I don't understand this kind of analysis. If a client asks a question, I won't know the answer. It's still not the right way to do this.
I have explained why Aisyah's offer, while kind, does not solve the underlying problem.

STRATEGY: PROPOSE. Hui Min has a very fair point. Just showing her the steps isn't enough if she can't answer questions on the analysis later. Forcing her to do it is wrong and will lead to weak work, which is her concern. Suresh seems determined to get this done, and he's more senior. It makes more sense for him to take on the complex part. I can propose that I brief him instead of Hui Min. This respects her concern and offers a more practical solution. I need to solve this so I can leave.

You're right, Hui Min. It's more than just following the steps. Suresh, maybe it would be better if I walk you through the analysis? You're more familiar with this kind of work. I can show you where everything is.
I've proposed a new solution that addresses Hui Min's concern and plays to Suresh's apparent confidence. I'll see how they respond.

STRATEGY: ACCEPT. Everyone else has refused. Aisyah's suggestion that I take over her work is the only option left to save the pitch. I'm furious with Hui Min and Daniel for their lack of teamwork, but the deadline is the most important thing. I'll take on the extra work myself because it has to be done. This is the only path forward.
Yes. Fine. Aisyah, walk me through it. Let's do it now before you have to go.
I have accepted Aisyah's offer as the final option. The next step is the handover.
